title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 719-724): Grothendieck is in the 'Longue Marche' setting, studying elliptic curves through their quotient by the inversion and through Kummer/abelian covers of the thrice-punctured line. On the previous page he wrote an S_3-equivariant embedding Psi of U_{0,3}=P^1-{0,1,oo} into the torus G_m^{{0,1,oo}}/G_m. Its image is the line x_0+x_1+x_oo=0, with Psi(z)=(-z,z-1,1). Equivariance checks: z->1-z swaps x_0 and x_1; z->1/z gives -(1,z-1,-z), which swaps x_0 and x_oo modulo scalars.

This page.
1. Assume 2 is invertible on S. Let X/S be an elliptic curve with its symmetry omega_X (the inversion x -> -x). Take the Legendre quotient Y = X/{1,omega_X}.
   - Y is a Brauer-Severi curve of relative dimension 1, i.e. a P^1-bundle over S.
   - S' is the image of the three nonzero 2-torsion points. It is finite étale of degree 3 over S.
   - The origin maps to a section of U = Y - S'.
   - Conversely, X is recovered as the double cover of Y branched along S' together with that section, up to the mu_2 of automorphisms.
2. Next, the pair (Y,S') is equivalent to S' alone, i.e. to an S_3-torsor T over S. Then:
   - Y = T ∧_{S_3} P^1_S, with S_3 permuting 0, 1, oo;
   - S' = T ∧_{S_3} {0,1,oo}_S;
   - U = T ∧_{S_3} (U_{0,3})_S.
3. Because Psi is S_3-equivariant, it twists. U embeds canonically into T ∧_{S_3} J^0_{(U_{0,3})_S} ≅ J^0_{U/S}. This is the generalized Jacobian of Y with reduced modulus S', i.e. the torus R_{S'/S}(G_m)/G_m. The map is the Rosenlicht-Serre Albanese / Abel-Jacobi map of U.
4. Composing with X -> Y gives a canonical morphism (318) X -> J^0_{U/S}. He identifies J^0_{U/S} with 'J^0_{X/S}' according to the conventions of p. 720. He announces that this map should be made explicit in terms of standard elliptic functions, but declines to do so on the next page.

Purpose (next page). The image of the origin is a section e in U(S) ⊂ J^0_{U/S}(S). Pulling back the multiplication-by-n isogeny tower of the torus along e gives a torsor under T_oo(J^0) ≅ T_oo(G_m) ⊗ M_0(S'/S). He identifies this with F_oo(X~/S), linking the arithmetic (Galois) action attached to X with Kummer theory of the Legendre-type invariant e (essentially lambda, 1-lambda twisted by T). This is part of describing M_{1,1}[1/2], viewed as a mu_2-gerbe over the S_3-quotient of the lambda-line, in terms of the (P^1, 0, 1, oo) picture and its Galois action.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One gap: the correspondence X <-> (Y,S',section) loses the automorphism -1. The 'correspondance' is a mu_2-gerbe, not an equivalence; this is presumably intended via 'muni de omega_X'.

The morphism (318) X -> J^0_{U/S} is only obviously defined on X minus the 2-torsion, via X -> Y ⊃ U. Extending it, or giving it a meaning, depends on the unstated 'conventions de p. 720' identifying J^0_{U/S} with J^0_{X/S}. Grothendieck leaves the explicit construction (via elliptic functions) undone.

ideas.what: Elliptic curves over S[1/2] correspond to (conic Y, degree-3 étale divisor S' ⊂ Y, section of Y-S'), via the quotient by inversion (Legendre theory)
ideas.modern_name: M_{1,1}[1/2] as a mu_2-gerbe over [ (P^1 - {0,1,oo}) / S_3 ]; Legendre lambda-line = M(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre/Jacobi classically; stack-theoretic form folklore (e.g. Deligne-Rapoport, Katz-Mazur level-2 theory)

ideas.what: Data (Y,S') equivalent to an S_3-torsor T, with Y = T ∧_{S_3} P^1 and S' = T ∧ {0,1,oo}
ideas.modern_name: Twisted forms of (P^1;0,1,oo) classified by H^1(S,S_3), since Aut(P^1,{0,1,oo}) = S_3

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant embedding of U_{0,3} into the torus G_m^3/G_m as the line x_0+x_1+x_oo=0, twisted to U ↪ J^0_{U/S} = R_{S'/S}G_m/G_m
ideas.modern_name: Albanese / generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht-Serre) of a twisted thrice-punctured line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht, Serre (Groupes algébriques et corps de classes)

ideas.what: Canonical morphism X -> J^0_{U/S} attached to an elliptic curve, to be made explicit by elliptic functions
ideas.modern_name: Map from an elliptic curve to the torus of its 2-torsion, composite of the quotient by ±1 with Abel-Jacobi; related to the 2-descent map x -> (x-e_i) in R_{S'/S}G_m / squares

missed.claim: Grothendieck canonically, and S_3-equivariantly over a general base S[1/2], links the elliptic curve to the torus R_{S'/S}G_m/G_m built from its 2-torsion scheme. He does this through the generalized Jacobian of the punctured conic X/±1. The point is to read the Galois action attached to X (next page: the torsor F_oo(X~/S)) as the Kummer torsor of a single section e of that torus. This is close to the classical 2-descent map x -> (x - e_i) and to Anderson-Ihara/Deligne treatments of P^1-{0,1,oo}. The explicit identification over a base, via twisting by the 2-torsion S_3-torsor, is a tidy formulation, but it is likely known in spirit.
missed.quote: plongé canoniquement dans T ∧_{S_3} J^0_{(M_{0,3})_S} ≃ J^0_{U/S}. Le plongement U ↪ J^0_{U/S} peut s'interpréter ici comme un morphisme canonique (318) X → J^0_{U/S}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a base-free, descent-theoretic packaging of 2-descent and Legendre-level Kummer torsors. It could be relevant to anabelian descriptions of M_{1,1} via the S_3-orbifold of the lambda-line, and to how the arithmetic Galois action on elliptic curves compares with that on P^1-{0,1,oo}. The explicit elliptic-function description is left unfinished.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but essentially classical reformulation: Legendre quotient, S_3-twisting, and the generalized Jacobian of the thrice-punctured line. The only mildly notable point is the intended canonical map X -> J^0_{U/S}, feeding a Kummer-torsor description of the Galois action. It resembles 2-descent and known P^1-{0,1,oo} theory, and its explicit form is left undone.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the insertion above 'correspondant' reads 'muni de omega_X'; omega_X is the inversion symmetry, and the quotient is X/{1,omega_X}.
'partant de là comme la solution locale' more plausibly reads 'partant de là comme de la situation locale/standard' (uncertain); the following formula is T ∧_{S_3} P^1_S.
The crossed-out part after T ∧_{S_3} P^1_S contains 'T ∧_{S_3} (M_{0,3})_S ... J^0', which was struck.
The subscript under the brace in (318) reads 'conventions de p. 720'.

Last line: 'qui doit être aussi[?] : construction[?] canonique' remains uncertain, but 'construction canonique' fits the continuation on p. 724 ('...ment, on a à expliciter en termes de fonctions elliptiques').
